events.title: How high will 10-year Treasury yield go before 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between November 11, 2025 and December 31, 2026. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent hawkish Federal Reserve communications and sticky inflation have lifted the 10-year Treasury yield to approximately 4.67–4.74 percent as of July 31, 2026, its highest level in months. Persistent price pressures, resilient labor market data, and elevated fiscal deficits are supporting a higher term premium and limiting expectations for aggressive policy easing. Market-implied odds reflect trader consensus that yields could test or exceed recent highs before year-end absent clear disinflationary progress. Key near-term catalysts include the August CPI release, upcoming FOMC minutes, and labor market reports that could shift rate-path expectations and influence long-end pricing through 2027.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Middle East tensions and sticky inflation have lifted the 10-year Treasury yield from early-2026 lows near 3.94% to around 4.58% as of mid-July, with markets now pricing a higher federal funds rate path and reduced odds of near-term easing. June CPI cooling to 3.5% year-over-year prompted a modest 2-basis-point pullback, while strong labor data and oil-price spikes from geopolitical risks have supported real yields. The July FOMC meeting and upcoming August PCE release, employment reports, and any escalation in energy markets remain key swing factors that could push the benchmark toward lower levels before year-end or reinforce the current range above 4%.

events.title: US 10Y Treasury yield above 5% by June 30?
events.description:
This is a market on whether the yield of the United States 10-Year Treasury Bond reaches greater than 5.000% between December 28 and market close on June 30, 2025.

If the yield of the US 10-Year T-Bond is greater than 5.000% at any time between between December 28, 2024 and market close on June 30 2025, this market will resolve to “Yes”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be investing.com's reporting found at https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/u.s.-10-year-bond-yield-historical-data. The resolution will be based on the values listed in the column labelled “High” in rows titled by dates within this market's timeframe.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 10-year Treasury yield surged to a March peak of 4.44% on March 27, 2026—its highest since July 2025—fueled by oil price spikes amid escalating geopolitical tensions, reigniting inflation fears and prompting traders to slash bets on Federal Reserve rate cuts from the current 3.50%-3.75% fed funds range. Yields retreated to 4.31% by the March 31 close as Fed Chair Powell's remarks tempered hike concerns, with the benchmark stabilizing near 4.30% on April 1 amid lighter trading volume. Polymarket trader consensus captured this volatility, pricing heightened uncertainty around inflation data and labor market strength; upcoming April nonfarm payrolls and CPI releases remain pivotal for post-deadline yield path expectations.
